story-031.source: git commit e04136d body + f279c62 body (verbatim). NO docs/ directory exists in this repo; CLAUDE.md and SolvencyDetermination.md contain NO story-031 material. Commit messages are the sole source of intent — no acceptance criteria were invented.
story-031.leg1_e04136d: "Wrap the previously-unwrapped phUSD.mint in _claimRewards with try/catch so a loss of mint authority banks the accrual into unclaimablePhUSDOf instead of reverting the whole claim and freezing the staker's principal path. Add the claimUnclaimablePhUSD pull path (re-mints, since nothing is custodied), new state + events, mirroring the story-029 stable-leg bank pattern."
story-031.leg2_f279c62: "Turn on the solc optimizer (runs=10000) with via_ir=false. PhlimboV3 drops from 24,945 B (unoptimized default build, 369 B over EIP-170) to 15,979 B (+8,597 B margin). Full suite stays green (365/365)... Deploying staging/mainnet with via_ir remains safe (no vm.warp on-chain)."

verdicts.story-031-leg1-banking: FAITHFUL + COMPLETE. The phUSD mint leg is wrapped in try/catch at src/PhlimboV3.sol:913, banking to unclaimablePhUSDOf[beneficiary] + totalUnclaimablePhUSD with a PhUSDMintFailed event. The claimUnclaimablePhUSD pull path (:644-650) exists, is nonReentrant, follows checks-effects-interactions (zeroes state at :647 BEFORE the re-mint at :649), and decrements totalUnclaimablePhUSD by exactly `amount` (never zeroed wholesale). State + events + interface declarations all landed. Verified: new suite PhlimboV3PhUSDMintBankTest 5/5 PASS; full suite 365/365 PASS (claim verified exactly).
verdicts.story-031-leg2-viair: FAITHFUL, and the EIP-170 claim is VERIFIED EXACTLY (built at HEAD: PhlimboV3 runtime 15,979 B, margin +8,597 B — byte-for-byte the commit's numbers). EIP-170 is genuinely RESOLVED, not merely flagged. Crucially, it is resolved by the OPTIMIZER and is INDEPENDENT of the via_ir setting: the via_ir=true build also fits comfortably (14,529 B, +10,047 B margin). The author's via_ir/vm.warp diagnosis is CORRECT and is a well-known solc-via_ir + cheatcode interaction; the on-chain safety argument (block.timestamp genuinely constant within a real tx) is sound. Residual assurance gap tracked as F-02.
verdicts.law1-override-check: NO Law-1 escalation from the story's core intent. Banking a failed mint cannot bank value never earned: unclaimablePhUSDOf is written ONLY in the catch at :915, crediting exactly `pendingPhUSDAmount` (the genuine accrual), and is read/zeroed only by the caller's own pull at :645-647. No admin/redirect writer exists. NO double-claim: all three _claimRewards callers realign phUSDDebt UNCONDITIONALLY after it returns (stake :715, withdraw :761, claim :808), so pending settles to zero whether the mint succeeded or banked — the banked amount is the sole record and can never be re-accrued. NO redistribution leak: phUSD emission is uncapped mint-on-demand (not drawn from a distributable pool), so unlike the stable leg no `:789`-style cap exclusion is needed — proven by test_bankedPhUSD_notRedistributed_toCostaker. The retrieval path does NOT recreate the bug one level down: claimUnclaimablePhUSD reverts while authority is still missing, but ONLY that function reverts — the bank stays intact and the principal path (stake/withdraw/claim) remains live. That is the correct claimUnclaimableStable recoverability semantic. One narrow value-stranding side effect on the migrator-delegated path IS surfaced as F-01.
verdicts.V3-M-05-completeness: COMPLETE — the incomplete-fix hypothesis is REFUTED BY EVIDENCE. All THREE legs are banked at HEAD. M-05's own two legs were closed by story-029 at the PREVIOUS baseline (e32588d), exactly as the run-10 incompleteFixFlag_phlimbo_ea_10 already recorded; the ONLY residual was the phUSD mint leg (tracked separately as V3-M-07), which story-031 now closes. The flag's stated closure condition — 'Verify the phUSD leg is banked (per V3-M-07 recommendation) before the fix can be considered complete' — is now SATISFIED.
verdicts.no-collapse-compliance: V3-M-05 and V3-M-07 are NOT conflated or collapsed, per V3-M-07's triageReason ('Distinct from V3-M-05, whose trigger is an EXTERNAL blocklisted recipient, not an owner action — do not conflate or collapse'). They remain two distinct entries with two distinct triggers, verified INDEPENDENTLY by two separate PoC replays, and are proposed closed SEPARATELY on separate evidence.

findings.specText: story-031 (commit e04136d): "Wrap the previously-unwrapped phUSD.mint in _claimRewards with try/catch so a loss of mint authority banks the accrual into unclaimablePhUSDOf instead of reverting the whole claim and freezing the staker's principal path. Add the claimUnclaimablePhUSD pull path (re-mints, since nothing is custodied)". Source comment at src/PhlimboV3.sol:909-912 asserts: "Credits the BENEFICIARY, mirroring the stable leg below." IPhlimboV3.sol PhUSDMintFailed NatSpec concedes the routing: "(the reward recipient, not necessarily the staked user — matches _claimRewards routing; under migrator delegation this is the migrator)". Counterpart intent in MigratorV2V3.sol:254-256: "Wiring prerequisite (b): phlimboV3.setMigrator(this)... Any V3 auto-claim (second pass only) lands here and is included in the deltas below."
findings.specSource: git commit e04136d body + src/PhlimboV3.sol:909-912 + src/interfaces/IPhlimboV3.sol PhUSDMintFailed NatSpec + src/MigratorV2V3.sol:254-256
findings.actualBehavior: The bank credits `beneficiary`, and under migrator delegation beneficiary == MigratorV2V3 (PhlimboV3.stake routes _claimRewards(user, msg.sender) at :708). MigratorV2V3 accounts for V3 auto-claim by BALANCE DELTA (`phUSDRewards = phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore`, :260) and forwards that delta to the user via _forward (:268). When the phUSD mint fails on a second-pass migrateOne, story-031's catch banks the accrual into PhlimboV3.unclaimablePhUSDOf[migrator] — but the migrator's phUSD balance never moves, so the delta reads 0, _forward forwards nothing, and the migration reports SUCCESS. The banked value is then unreachable: MigratorV2V3 has NO function that can call PhlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD() (its own claimUnclaimable(token) at :302 pays only from its OWN `unclaimable` mapping, which was never credited; withdrawAll() at :318 sweeps only balances it HOLDS). PhlimboV3 has no admin/redirect writer for unclaimablePhUSDOf (verified: written only at :915 and :647), and emergencyTransfer (:360-365) sweeps only the phUSD BALANCE — the banked phUSD was never minted, so there is nothing to sweep.
findings.deviation: Story-031's stated goal is to stop a mint failure from bricking the principal path. On the self-service path it achieves exactly that. On the migrator-delegated path it converts a LOUD, self-healing failure into a SILENT, in-contract-permanent one: pre-fix, the mint revert bricked the migrate pass (V3-M-07's brick — bad, but recoverable by restoring mint authority and retrying); post-fix, the pass succeeds while the user's phUSD accrual is silently stranded under the migrator's address. This also defeats MigratorV2V3's own documented delta-capture assumption at :254-256 ('included in the deltas below'), which story-031 did not update.
findings.impactAssessment: Honest severity LOW — tested against Medium and REFUTED. (1) Compound trigger: requires phUSD mint-authority revocation, which the human already triaged WONT-FIX on V3-M-07 as owner-privileged and self-inflicted ('cutting off nose to spite the face'), AND an active migrator second-pass on a user who already holds a V3 position (stake only calls _claimRewards `if (userDetails.amount > 0)`). (2) Scope: strands REWARD ACCRUAL only — principal is unaffected and, thanks to this very story, now flows freely. (3) Recoverable out-of-band: phUSD is mint-on-demand, so the phUSD authority can mint the shortfall to the user directly; the loss is in-contract, not absolute. Not a Law-1 escalation: no attacker path, no unprivileged trigger, no theft. Surfaced rather than dropped per Law 1 recall-beats-tidiness, and because it is a genuine NEW consequence introduced by this story's own intent. NOTE the pattern gap is shared with the story-029 stable bank (unclaimableStableOf[migrator] is equally unreachable by the migrator) — but that one is strictly BETTER off, because the stable bank holds REAL tokens that emergencyTransfer CAN sweep (:354 NatSpec says so explicitly). The phUSD bank has no such backstop, so story-031's mirror of the stable pattern is not a faithful mirror in the recovery dimension.
findings.recommendation: Cheapest fix: in MigratorV2V3._migrateOne, after phlimboV3.stake(...), call phlimboV3.claimUnclaimablePhUSD() inside a try/catch (or read PhlimboV3.unclaimablePhUSDOf(address(this)) and pull when non-zero) so a banked accrual is re-minted into the migrator and picked up by the existing delta+_forward accounting. Alternative: add an onlyOwner reassignment on PhlimboV3 that moves a bank entry from the migrator to the underlying user. Minimal alternative: accept and document that the migrator-beneficiary phUSD bank is out-of-band-settled, and correct the now-false MigratorV2V3:254-256 comment claiming V3 auto-claim is 'included in the deltas below'.
findings.crossRef: V3-M-07 (27e83ab2, wont-fix — same mint-revocation trigger gates this); V3-L-11 (b9de837c — migrator-as-beneficiary routing class at MigratorV2V3.sol:250)

findings.specText: story-031 (commit f279c62): "via_ir is deliberately OFF for unit/local builds: under via_ir the optimizer caches block.timestamp within a frame (a valid on-chain invariant), which collapses the repeated `vm.warp(block.timestamp + ...)` calls some tests use for cumulative time progression -> time appears frozen, accrual reads 0. The contracts are correct; this is purely a test<->cheatcode interaction. Deploying staging/mainnet with via_ir remains safe (no vm.warp on-chain)." foundry.toml:6-15 repeats this verbatim.
findings.specSource: git commit f279c62 body + foundry.toml:6-15 comment
findings.actualBehavior: The story's own text explicitly contemplates a via_ir PRODUCTION deploy ('Deploying staging/mainnet with via_ir remains safe') while pinning via_ir=false for every build this repo performs. That deploy vehicle exists and is already configured the other way: lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml sets `via_ir = true` (with optimizer_runs = 10000) and remaps `@phlimbo-ea/=lib/phlimbo-ea/src/`, compiling phlimbo-ea contracts FROM SOURCE. phStaging is the established deployment vehicle for this project — it already deploys Phlimbo V1/V2 (imports @phlimbo-ea/Phlimbo.sol, @phlimbo-ea/PhlimboV2.sol, @phlimbo-ea/MigratorV1V2.sol). The two pipelines emit materially different bytecode, verified empirically at HEAD: legacy+optimizer = 15,979 B runtime, via_ir+optimizer = 14,529 B runtime (a 1,450 B / ~9% codegen delta). phlimbo-ea's 365-test suite — including story-031's own new PhlimboV3PhUSDMintBankTest — only ever executes the legacy bytecode. Verified that CI does NOT close this gap: .github/workflows/test.yml sets FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci, but no [profile.ci] section exists, so it inherits default (confirmed by `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci forge config`: optimizer=true, optimizer_runs=10000, via_ir=false).
findings.deviation: Not a deviation from the story's letter — the implementation does exactly what the story says. The gap is in the story's own reasoning: it justifies via_ir=false with an argument that covers ONE specific divergence (timestamp caching) and then generalises to 'deploying with via_ir remains safe' without validating the via_ir-compiled bytecode at all. If PhlimboV3 ships through phStaging (the established path), the audited and tested semantics are not the deployed semantics.
findings.impactAssessment: Honest severity LOW / QA — an ASSURANCE gap, not a demonstrated bug. Deliberately NOT overstated: no behavioural divergence between the two pipelines was demonstrated, and the author is RIGHT on the substance. Specifically confirmed in the author's favour: (a) the via_ir + vm.warp(block.timestamp + X) diagnosis is a real, well-known solc-via_ir/cheatcode interaction, not a contract defect; (b) the on-chain safety argument is sound — block.timestamp IS genuinely constant within a real transaction, so THIS divergence provably cannot manifest on-chain; (c) EIP-170 is genuinely RESOLVED, not merely flagged — the commit's numbers reproduce byte-for-byte at HEAD (15,979 B runtime, +8,597 B margin) and the 365/365 green claim verifies exactly. Also worth recording: EIP-170 is resolved by the OPTIMIZER and is fully INDEPENDENT of via_ir — the via_ir build fits even more comfortably (14,529 B, +10,047 B margin) — so via_ir=false is NOT load-bearing for EIP-170 and can be revisited freely without reopening the size problem. The residual risk is the generic one: via_ir is a distinct Yul codegen pipeline with its own historical miscompilation record, and PhlimboV3 currently has zero test coverage of the bytecode that would actually be deployed. Mitigating context: PhlimboV3 is NOT yet wired into phStaging (no PhlimboV3 reference exists anywhere in that repo), so this is a PROSPECTIVE hazard to close BEFORE the V3 deploy story, not a live one.
findings.recommendation: Preferred (removes the root cause and restores test/deploy parity): refactor the affected tests off `vm.warp(block.timestamp + X)` onto an explicit absolute-time accumulator (`uint256 t = block.timestamp; t += X; vm.warp(t);`), which is immune to the frame-caching interaction, then re-enable via_ir so builds and tests match the phStaging deploy pipeline. Alternative (keeps the workaround, closes the gap): add a `[profile.viair]` mirroring phStaging's settings (optimizer=true, optimizer_runs=10000, via_ir=true) and run the suite under it in CI, excluding only the known warp-loop tests — this at least exercises the deployed codegen. Minimum: pin the deploy pipeline explicitly (assert phStaging compiles PhlimboV3 with the same settings the suite validates) and record the divergence as an accepted, documented risk before the V3 deploy story lands.
findings.crossRef: lib/phoenix-phase-2-staging/foundry.toml (via_ir = true, @phlimbo-ea remapping); .github/workflows/test.yml (FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci inherits default — verified, no gap)
